cards.back: A data display that shows the variability of a data set along a number line using the five-number summary: minimum, Q1, median, Q3, maximum.
The five key values that make up a box-and-whisker plot: least value, first quartile (Q1), median (Q2), third quartile (Q3), greatest value.
Values that divide an ordered data set into four equal parts. Q1 is the median of the lower half, Q2 is the overall median, Q3 is the median of the upper half.

cards.front: Make a box-and-whisker plot for the ages: 24, 30, 30, 22, 25, 22, 18, 25, 28, 30, 25, 27.
cards.back: Order: 18,22,22,24,25,25,25,27,28,30,30,30. Min=18, Q1=23, Median=25, Q3=29, Max=30. Box from 23 to 29, median line at 25, whiskers to 18 and 30.

cards.front: How is the first quartile (Q1) found?
cards.back: Q1 is the median of the lower half of the ordered data. If the overall median falls on a data value, exclude it from both halves.
The difference between the third quartile and the first quartile: $$\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$$ It measures the spread of the middle 50% of the data.

cards.front: What percentage of the data lies in each whisker of a box-and-whisker plot?
cards.back: About 25% of the data lies in each whisker. The box contains the middle 50% of the data.

cards.front: How can you tell if a distribution is [[imp:skewed left]] from a box-and-whisker plot?
cards.back: The left whisker is longer than the right whisker. Most of the data are on the right side of the plot.

cards.front: How can you tell if a distribution is [[imp:skewed right]] from a box-and-whisker plot?
cards.back: The right whisker is longer than the left whisker. Most of the data are on the left side of the plot.

cards.front: What does a symmetric box-and-whisker plot look like?
cards.back: The whiskers are about the same length, and the median is centered in the middle of the box.

cards.front: Find the range and IQR for song lengths: min=160, Q1=220, median=250, Q3=280, max=300.
How do you compare two data sets using double box-and-whisker plots?
cards.back: Compare medians (center), IQRs and ranges (spread), and whisker lengths (shape). The set with the longer box or longer whiskers is more spread out.

cards.front: In a double box-and-whisker plot, your class has a higher median but a smaller IQR than your friend's class. What does this mean?
cards.back: Your class performed better on average (higher median) and had more consistent scores (smaller IQR). Your friend's class had more variability in scores.

cards.front: Entrée prices: min=8.75, Q1=10.5, median=13.25, Q3=14.75, max=18.25. What is the IQR?
cards.back: IQR = 14.75 − 10.5 = 4.25 dollars. The middle 50% of entrées are within a $4.25 price range.

cards.front: In the entrée price plot, the right whisker is longer than the left whisker. What is the shape?
cards.back: Skewed right. There are some higher-priced entrées pulling the upper end of the data.
